supersedes.priorClaim: "oracle-judged" — V9 proved the frozen ENGINE (lending_accrual.py) byte-equivalent to the monorepo oracle, but the TS TRANSFORM the standalone rewrote (DataPlaneEngine.buildLendingJob / marketPayload / commonWindow) was NEVER differentially run against its original, because the monorepo had no installed dependencies. The adjective 'oracle-judged' was true of the engine, a half-step ahead of the transform.

newState.claim: the standalone TRANSFORM is byte-identical to its ORIGINAL — the monorepo's exact Runner.legSeries (yield branch) + Runner.commonWindow, run in a sandbox on identical pinned captured snapshots (5 real lending pools), produce per-market series (apyBase·tvl·turnover) + a common window BYTE-IDENTICAL to the standalone rewrite. 'oracle-judged' is now true of the PORT, not just the engine.
newState.asteriskDisposition: RETIRED AT THE LETTER for the lending transform: the D-DIFF asterisk V9 carried (transform not differentially tested) is closed on byte evidence a skeptic can reproduce (re-run script/transform-differential.ts against the sandbox). The differential was direction-blind and prepared to lose (a seeded flattering divergence is caught); it MATCHED.
newState.scopeHonesty: the comparison is the LOAD-BEARING per-market series the accrual consumes + the window; the full monorepo Job's RWA scaffolding (pegMark, benchmarks, redemption/issuer/assetClass, seed/nTrials) feeds the FULL accrual.py and is out-of-scope-by-construction for the slim lending path — named, not hidden. A whole-Job byte-diff is impossible (different shapes, different sidecars); the transform slice is the honest, load-bearing comparison.
